sections_inspected: First Principles, PDF p. 2, paragraphs beginning “A starting point might be a conceptual purification” and “This politics must start from the observation”
scope_outcomes.criterion: A substantive passage in which the citing author defends, reconstructs, criticizes, applies, or surveys a proposition associated with Max Weber
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected passage explicitly attributes to Weber the proposition that class is fractured by the material interests arising from the market positions of its component parts, and uses that proposition in Riley’s argument for a materialist political strategy.
limitations: The source is a short two-page article and does not identify the specific Weber work or edition.
This finding concerns the inspected source, not Riley’s complete reception of Weber.
